slides.headline: AFTER PAYING $1.5 BILLION FOR PIRATING BOOKS, AI COMPANIES JUST STARTED SHREDDING THE PHYSICAL COPIES INSTEAD
AN AI COMPANY SLICED OPEN THOUSANDS OF BOOKS WITH A HYDRAULIC CUTTER
slides.body: Anthropic — the company behind the AI chatbot Claude — bought countless used books from resellers. They used a hydraulic cutting machine to neatly remove every page, then scanned them all with industrial-grade imaging equipment

slides.headline: A JUDGE RULED IT COMPLETELY LEGAL
slides.body: Anthropic already paid a $1.5 billion settlement for pirating digital books from authors. So the industry switched to buying physical copies instead. A legal rule called first-sale doctrine says once you buy something, you can do whatever you want with it — and a judge called scanning the pages "transformative" and protected under fair use

slides.headline: ONE BOOK SELLER QUIETLY HANDED AI COMPANIES UP TO A MILLION BOOKS PER ORDER
slides.body: A book database called ISBNdb used to help libraries and bookshops find titles. Now it helps AI companies bulk-buy 1,000 to 1 million books at a time. It promises to keep every buyer's name secret — and pitches books printed before 2022 as guaranteed free of AI-written junk that already pollutes the internet

slides.headline: THESE COMPANIES SPENT MILLIONS HUNTING CLEAN TEXT YOUR BUSINESS ALREADY HAS
slides.body: They're buying and destroying physical books because they need real human writing that AI hasn't touched. Your business already sits on years of it — emails, notes, procedures, customer calls. Most owners don't realize their own records could power an AI that handles half their daily busywork without hiring anyone
